standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of submodules of a finite module over a Noetherian ring

standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the integral closure of R is a finite R-module once it is contained in a finite one.

core_obligations: Let R' and S' be the integral closures of R and of the Laurent ring in their fraction fields, and note that R' is contained in S', which itself sits inside the Laurent ring of the fraction field because that is normal (proof lines 45458-45461).

Assume S' is a finite module over the Laurent ring, with finitely many generators f_i, and write each f_i as a finite Laurent polynomial in z with coefficients a_{ij} in the fraction field (proof lines 45462-45463).

For each x in R' express x as a combination of the f_i with coefficients in the Laurent ring and deduce that x lies in the finite R-module generated by the a_{ij}; Noetherianity then makes R' finite over R (proof lines 45464-45470).
proof_roadmap: Nest the two integral closures and bound S' inside a Laurent ring (proof lines 45457-45461).
Show R' sits in a finite R-module by reading off the coefficient set of the Laurent expansions (proof lines 45462-45471).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a Noetherian domain R, if the Laurent ring R[z, z to the minus one] is N-1, then R is N-1 as well (statement lines 45451-45455). The proof does not exhibit a finite generating set for the integral closure directly: it nests the two integral closures, uses normality of the Laurent ring over the fraction field to bound S' inside it, writes finitely many Laurent expansions of the generators, and shows that R' lies in the finite R-module generated by the finitely many coefficients, invoking Noetherianity at the end (proof lines 45457-45471). Choosing the coefficient module as the witness of finiteness is the substance, and the author writes the reduction out. H2.
